messages:
Leah (SRE): Quick follow-up from the 3/21 high-p95 incidents. We had recurring short spikes across inference nodes; p95 jumped to ~1.7s for ~10m windows vs baseline ~150ms. Need remediation owners, a short-term SLO tweak, and a repeatable dashboard/watchbook so this doesn't surprise ops again.

Diego (Platform): Agree. Two parallel tracks: mitigation (graceful degradation + routing fallbacks) and permanent fix (cache stability + request shaping). What SLO tweak are you thinking?

Leah (SRE): Proposed emergency SLO (2 weeks): public-hosted p95 <= 300ms (was 200ms). Also add an error-budget hold rule: if 72h burn-rate > 1.3 then pause non-critical automated deploys. We keep p99 target unchanged.

Sam (Service Owner): Can we avoid loosening SLO if we do graceful degradation? For enterprise routes we must maintain SLA. My suggestion: keep SLO but enable degraded-path (reduced-quality embeddings + async fallback) for low-priority clients and non-enterprise API keys.

Maya (Product): That sounds reasonable. Need a clear customer-impact matrix so sales/support know which tenants get degraded. Diego, can you add a label-based routing rule?

Diego (Platform): Yes. I can add label-based routing and a 2% default canary to quantized variants immediately. Escalation policy: if 24h burn-rate > 1.5 expand to 10%.

Leah (SRE): Action items (short):
- Leah: Add burn-rate alerting + playbook snippet to SLO dashboard (today)
- Diego: Implement 2% canary fallback + label routing (today)
- Sam: Draft degradation policy mapping (end of week)
- Diego & Sam: Decide enterprise exclusion list (3 days)
- Leah: Temporary SLO adjustment announcement template for sales/support (tomorrow)

Sam (Service Owner): I'll own the degradation policy draft. For endpoints: /generate, /chat, /embed. Will list which features to disable per endpoint.

Diego (Platform): Created dashboard panel and alert: link https://dash.redwoodinternal.com/d/slo/latency-burn (panel id: p95-burn). PromQL snippet I added to dashboard: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service, route))

Leah (SRE): I also updated the runbook: playbook section 'latency spike -> apply degraded route -> notify owners -> revert after 24h stable'. Adding CSV export for top callers so product can triage heavy clients.

ops-bot: Calendar event created: "SLO remediation check-in" Mon 09:00 PT. Alert group: p95 burn-rate > 1.2, notify #eng-sre + oncall.

Maya (Product): I'll prepare the customer comm template and coordinate with sales for any enterprise exceptions.

Sam (Service Owner): Quick note: I'll collaborate with Diego on safe rollout to ensure no config drift. ETA for initial draft: 2 business days.

Diego (Platform): I'll keep the fallback rule scoped to non-enterprise keys until Sam confirms the list. Posting PR for routing changes in 2 hours.

Leah (SRE): We'll reconvene after the first 24h of mitigation to see if error budget burn reduces. If not, we escalate permanent fixes (cache TTL hardening, request shaping at edge).

Maya (Product): Thanks all. Please put your action items into the postmortem tracker and tag them with owner+due date. I'll track customer comms.

Leah (SRE): Copy that. I'll update the tracker by EOD and paste the link here.

Diego (Platform): PR opened: https://git.internal/routing/PR-482. Comments welcome.

Leah (SRE): Closing notes: prefer degradation over loosening SLAs; temporary SLO change is a last resort but policy approved for 2 weeks if needed. Follow-up thread update by EOD tomorrow.
